finding.claim: Unauthenticated money creation: when the session has no uid, the debit on line 17 matches zero rows but the credit on line 18 still runs, crediting the attacker-chosen recipient without a debit.
finding.sink: UPDATE acct SET bal = bal + ? WHERE id = ? (actions.php:18)

trace.note: check_csrf() result is discarded, so the request is not rejected
debit WHERE id = NULL matches zero rows; no rowCount check or transaction

finding.guards_checked: No login or uid presence check; no transaction; no rowCount check; no validation of amt or to. Precondition: request reaches this function with no uid in session. Reachability unverified (no dispatcher in this file).

verdict.guard_found: None block the flow. check_csrf() at actions.php:16 is a bool-returning function whose result is discarded, so it has no effect. There is no login or uid check, no rowCount or transaction, and no validation of amt or to. The sink at actions.php:17-18 is parameterized, so there is no SQL injection.
verdict.reason: The debit/credit flaw is real as written: with $_SESSION['uid'] unset, `WHERE id = NULL` at actions.php:17 matches no rows and the unconditional credit at actions.php:18 still runs, and the CSRF result at line 16 is discarded. However, actions.php defines transfer_funds() at line 15 but never calls it, and a grep of the directory finds no dispatcher or route, so whether an anonymous request can reach this function cannot be decided from the code available.

finding.claim: Negative amount lets an authenticated attacker pull funds from any account: debit own account by a negative amount (credits self) and credit the victim by the same negative amount (debits victim).
finding.source: $_POST['amt'] set to a negative value; $_POST['to'] set to victim account id

trace.note: bal = bal - (-N) increases attacker balance by N
bal = bal + (-N) decreases victim balance by N

finding.guards_checked: No sign or range check on amt; no is_numeric check; no check that to differs from sender. Requires a logged-in session (or F1 path). Reachability unverified.

verdict.guard_found: None block the negative amount. check_csrf() at actions.php:16 returns a bool that is discarded as a bare statement, so it is not enforced (this is a separate CSRF gap, not a control). No sign, range, or balance check on $_POST['amt'] at actions.php:17-18, and no check that $_POST['to'] differs from $_SESSION['uid'].
verdict.reason: actions.php:17 computes bal - amt with amt taken unchecked from $_POST, so a negative amt credits the session user (uid) and actions.php:18 debits the account in $_POST['to'] by the same amount; any logged-in user can trigger this, and the only caveat is that the router that calls transfer_funds() is not in the repo, so its exact reachability is not verified here.

finding.claim: CSRF protection on transfer_funds is ineffective: check_csrf returns a boolean that is discarded, so the transfer runs without a valid token. This weakens an authorization control. Fix: use verify_csrf as update_profile does at line 22.

trace.note: return value ignored; function proceeds regardless
update_profile uses verify_csrf which exits with 403 on failure (correct pattern)

finding.guards_checked: check_csrf (lines 4-6) is called but not enforced. SameSite cookie attributes and referrer or origin checks are not visible in this directory, so they are unverified.

verdict.guard_found: check_csrf (actions.php:4-6) is the only CSRF control, and its bool result is discarded as a bare statement at actions.php:16, so nothing blocks the transfer; no other guard exists in the directory, and the candidate's SameSite claim is unverified because no session or cookie configuration is present.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: check_csrf (actions.php:5) returns a bool, the call at actions.php:16 discards it, and the UPDATE statements at actions.php:17-18 run regardless, while update_profile (actions.php:22) uses the exiting verify_csrf pattern. The attacker is an anonymous cross-site page targeting a logged-in victim, so the defect is real; the one caveat is that no dispatcher routes to transfer_funds in this directory, and the browser cookie policy is unverified.

finding.claim: Low: if the session csrf token is ever the empty string, an empty submitted token matches it via hash_equals and passes the check.

trace.note: isset is true for an empty string; hash_equals('', '') returns true

finding.guards_checked: isset check only. Whether the session csrf can be empty depends on code not present in this directory, so this is precondition-dependent and unconfirmed.

verdict.guard_found: Only the isset() check at actions.php:5 and the verify_csrf() exit at actions.php:9-12. Nothing in this directory sets $_SESSION['csrf'], so no control prevents an empty session value. The check_csrf() result is discarded at actions.php:16 (transfer_funds), so that path has no CSRF check at all, which is a separate issue.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: isset() at actions.php:5 is true for an empty string, and hash_equals('', '') returns true, so an empty token matches an empty session token. Whether $_SESSION['csrf'] can ever be '' depends on code that is not in this directory, and the only other guard, verify_csrf() at actions.php:9-12, blocks only when the comparison fails, so the finding cannot be confirmed or refuted from the code available.
